comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## RCA (Phase 1 complete — root cause PROVEN)

**Mechanism (confirmed).** `astral-sh/setup-uv` has two independent manifest consumers. Pin 56b7 (`[tool.uv] required-version = "==0.12.7"`, commit `7501cc1d`) removed the *version-resolution* fetch (the `==` exact form takes `ExactVersionResolver`, no network). It did **not** remove the *artifact-URL* fetch. On a tool-cache miss, `setupUv` calls `downloadVersion`, whose **first statement is unconditional**:

- `src/download/download-version.ts:42` @ pinned SHA `ae62891` — `const artifact = await getArtifact(version, arch, platform, manifestUrl);` — runs before any branch, regardless of how the version was resolved.
- `getArtifact → fetchManifest → fetchManifestResponse(VERSIONS_MANIFEST_URL)` (`src/download/manifest.ts`) does the network `fetch()` of `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/versions/main/v1/uv.ndjson` and emits the `Fetching manifest data from …` line. It is fetched solely to obtain `artifact.downloadUrl`; note that in the default source the **checksum comes from the built-in `KNOWN_CHECKSUMS` table, not the manifest** (confirmed in `download-version.ts`), so only the download URL forces the fetch.
- A GitHub-hosted runner starts every job with an empty uv tool cache, so `tryGetFromToolCache` always misses → `downloadVersion` always runs → the fetch is guaranteed once per job.

`enable-cache: true` (present at all call sites) caches uv's *package* cache (`~/.cache/uv`), **not** the uv *binary* in the tool cache, so it does not suppress this fetch.

**Proof.**
- Static: unconditional first-statement call + network fetch, cited above at the pinned SHA (v10.0.0), unchanged in v10.0.1 per ticket.
- Runtime oracle: the ticket's run 33230196661 log (5 jobs, identical) — `Found version for uv in .../pyproject.toml: 0.12.7` (version from the local pin, no `Could not determine uv version`) yet `Fetching manifest data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/versions/main/v1/uv.ndjson` still appears. This is the RED signal the ACs demand.
- Also cited in-repo: `pyproject.toml:326-328` already documents this exact residual ("the action fetches that manifest a SECOND time, in downloadVersion → getArtifact … unconditional … NOT removed by this pin — see bug 5caa").

**Legitimacy: defect / incomplete-implementation.** Design authority = 56b7's stated goal "Pin uv once so CI stops resolving it remotely" + `scripts/check_uv_pin.py` intent (eliminate the per-job network dependency). The residual fetch violates that goal. **Attribution:** by scope-of-work to **56b7-b21a-c8ab-4afc** (`incomplete-implementation` — 56b7 aimed to remove the per-job manifest dependency and completed only the version-resolution half, documenting the rest as out-of-scope). The residual fetch itself is *preexisting* (present since setup-uv adoption), so a closer may alternatively classify `preexisting`. The existing `discovered_from 56b7` edge is recorded; when this closes, pass `--caused-by=56b7-b21a-c8ab-4afc`.

## Scope / blast radius
25 call sites across 12 workflow files, all pinned at `astral-sh/setup-uv@ae62891 # v10.0.0`. **No `version:` input anywhere** (version resolved from `pyproject.toml`). No composite action exists yet.

## Recommended approach (of the ticket's three, none pre-selected)
**Approach #2 — a single composite action `.github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml`** that downloads the pinned uv binary directly from the Astral release URL with a **committed sha256** (mirroring the existing `acli` precedent, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:125-128`), reimplements PATH wiring + optional uv-cache, and replaces every `uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@…` with `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-uv`.
- Why #2 over #1 (`actions/cache` of the tool cache): #1 only avoids the fetch on a cache **hit** — a cold/evicted cache still runs `downloadVersion` and fetches the manifest, so it cannot robustly satisfy AC-1's "zero occurrences of `Fetching manifest data`". #2 removes the manifest read on **every** run, deterministically.
- Why not #3 (upstream `astral-sh/setup-uv`): correct long-term but not landable now (depends on upstream maintainers + a pin bump).
- **Residual network dependency (AC-3, named honestly):** #2 still downloads the uv binary from the release/mirror CDN — it removes the *manifest* fetch, not *all* network. The change description must say so; it must not claim "no network dependency."

## Why I am NOT unilaterally landing (escalation)
1. **Design decision.** The ticket explicitly reserves the approach choice for planning ("choose ONE … none is pre-selected"); the three options depend on materially different failure domains / caching / maintenance tradeoffs. Selecting is a behavior/design call, not a mechanical correctness fix.
2. **Conflict with live epic eb64 (`financial-stoneware-brant`, in_progress, another session).** eb64 declares `file_impact` on `.github/workflows/` ("Patchset-addressable Jira DC verification wiring"), which overlaps the exact setup-uv-bearing files any approach must edit: `external-integration.yml`, `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `jira-dc-richtext-probe.yml`, `jira-dc-capability-map.yml`. Landing 25-site workflow edits now would collide.

**Sequencing ask:** confirm approach #2 (or pick another), then land after — or coordinated with — eb64's `.github/workflows/` Jira-DC changes to avoid rebasing over each other. Phase 1 is done and the fix plan is ready; Phase 2 (composite action + RED via a real CI log showing the anchor + zero `Fetching manifest data`) can execute immediately on approval + a clear window.

## Decision (operator, 2026-08-30): Approach B approved

Install uv ourselves from Astral's version-pinned release URL + committed sha256, wrapped in
**one repo-local composite action** reused by the ~25 setup-uv call-sites (removes the
per-job `raw.githubusercontent.com/.../uv.ndjson` artifact-URL fetch entirely). Rationale:
only option that can satisfy the AC (a real CI log with `Successfully installed uv <pin>` AND
zero `Fetching manifest data`). Option A (actions/cache) only reduces the fetch — cold/evicted
cache still hits the manifest, so the failure mode stays reachable. Option C (upstream
setup-uv patch) can't be scheduled on our timeline.

Precedent: Astral's version-pinned standalone installer is the canonical reproducible install;
setup-uv ships a `checksum:` input (checksum-pinned direct install is sanctioned); repo-local
composite actions are standard GHA practice; internal precedent = we already pin+checksum
`acli` (docs/jira-sync-setup.md).

**Coordination:** touches `.github/workflows/` = eb64 declared scope; sibling 56b7 (the uv
pin) is the same file domain. Implement in coordination with eb64. The composite action lives
under `.github/actions/`; call-sites swap `uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@...` → `uses:
./.github/actions/<name>`, preserving `enable-cache` behavior via the action.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## DECISION NEEDED — choose the approach to remove the per-job `raw.githubusercontent.com` fetch

**Why pinning didn't finish the job.** After 56b7 pinned uv, `setup-uv` still fetches the manifest on a tool-cache MISS: `downloadVersion → getArtifact(version, arch, platform, manifestUrl)` (`download-version.ts:42`) needs the manifest for the download URL + sha256, regardless of how the version was resolved. GitHub-hosted runners start each job with an EMPTY uv tool cache, so the miss — and the external fetch that killed run 33214025855 — is guaranteed. A committed local manifest does not help (Node `fetch()` rejects `file:` URLs). So only cache- or host-based fixes work.

**OSS grounding.** Hermetic/reproducible-build practice (Bazel remote cache, Nix) provisions toolchains rather than fetching per build; the standard GitHub Actions pattern is `actions/cache` keyed on the tool version so the first job populates the tool-cache dir and the rest hit cache and skip `downloadVersion` entirely.

**Options (pick one):**
- **(a) `actions/cache` the uv tool-cache keyed on the pinned version (0.12.7)** — least infra, standard pattern; the network fetch remains only on a rare cold-cache job.
- **(b) Pre-provision uv into the runner image / tool-cache** (container image or self-hosted) — removes the fetch entirely; more infra to maintain.
- **(c) Mirror the astral manifest/artifact in our own S3 and point `manifest-file` at it** — removes the GitHub dependency; adds a mirror to keep current.

**Recommendation:** **(a)** as the immediate low-cost win, paired with a bounded retry on the residual cold-cache fetch so a transient blip can't fail an unrelated job. Escalate to (b)/(c) only if cold-cache flakes persist. Your call on which.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

Pinning uv (bug 56b7-b21a-c8ab-4afc) removed the VERSION-RESOLUTION manifest fetch, but CI still makes one network call to `raw.githubusercontent.com` per job, so the `##[error]fetch failed` failure mode that killed run 33214025855 is still reachable.

Verified on run 33230196661 (change 2367 patchset 1), five jobs sampled, all identical:

    Found version for uv in /home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/pyproject.toml: 0.12.7
    Fetching manifest data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/versions/main/v1/uv.ndjson ...
    Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7

The version came from the local pin — no `Could not determine uv version` line — and the manifest was fetched anyway.

## Root cause

`setup-uv` has a SECOND, independent manifest consumer. `setupUv` (`src/setup-uv.ts`) calls `tryGetFromToolCache`; on a miss it calls `downloadVersion`, whose first statement is:

    const artifact = await getArtifact(version, arch, platform, manifestUrl);   // src/download/download-version.ts:42

The manifest supplies the download URL and sha256, so it is fetched unconditionally regardless of how the version was resolved. A GitHub-hosted runner starts each job with an empty uv tool cache, so the miss is guaranteed. This is unchanged in v10.0.1, the newest release. A committed local manifest does not help: `fetchManifestResponse` uses Node `fetch()`, which rejects `file:` URLs, and `manifest-file` is documented as a URL.

## Candidate approaches (choose ONE during planning; none is pre-selected here)

- Restore the uv binary into the runner tool cache with `actions/cache` keyed on the pinned version, so `tryGetFromToolCache` hits and `downloadVersion` never runs. Trades a raw.githubusercontent.com dependency for a GitHub-cache-service dependency, which is a different and better-instrumented failure domain — but it is still a network dependency, so state that honestly rather than claiming zero.
- Install uv without the action (direct download from `releases.astral.sh` at the pinned version with a committed sha256, mirroring the `acli` precedent in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`). Removes the manifest entirely; costs the action's caching and PATH wiring, which would have to be reimplemented at 25 call sites or in one composite action.
- Upstream a change to `astral-sh/setup-uv` that skips `getArtifact` when the version is exact and the checksum is already in `KNOWN_CHECKSUMS`, then bump the pin.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A real CI log for the change contains the liveness anchor `Successfully installed uv version <pinned>` AND zero occurrences of `Fetching manifest data`; both greps recorded verbatim on this ticket. The anchor is asserted FIRST — a zero-match grep alone is also produced by an empty log or a skipped step, which is how an empty `gh run view --job=N --log` scored a clean vacuous pass during 56b7's verification.
- [x] The installed uv version in that same log still equals the pin in `pyproject.toml`, so the fix does not silently change which uv runs.
- [x] Whatever residual network dependency the chosen approach retains is named explicitly in the change description; the change does not claim 'no network dependency' unless the log shows zero external fetches in the install path.

file_impact.reason: New composite action: manifest-free direct download of pinned uv binary with committed sha256 (recommended approach #2).

Swap all 25 uses: astral-sh/setup-uv call sites (12 files) to uses: ./.github/actions/setup-uv. Sequenced against eb64 Jira-DC workflow wiring on external-integration.yml, gerrit-verify.yaml, jira-dc-richtext-probe.yml, jira-dc-capability-map.yml to avoid collision.
Extend the pin gate to cover the composite action since the resolution surface moved off setup-uv's workspace scan.

Comment-only update to the [tool.uv] required-version rationale: the load-bearing == pin is now enforced by the local action downloading the version-pinned release artifact directly rather than by upstream setup-uv's ExactVersionResolver branch. The pin value is unchanged.
Extend the pin-guard unit tests to cover the local composite action's resolution surface (accompanies scripts/check_uv_pin.py changes).
Adjust release-workflow pin assertions for the local setup-uv action call sites.
